extracted.intended_audience: researchers (OSF users) considering preregistration or registered reports
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researchers on the benefits, features, and common concerns of preregistering study plans (and using Registered Reports) on the Open Science Framework. Helps decide whether and how to create/upate a preregistration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shows Credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: (Pre)registration signifies a dedication to methodological rigor and transparency, establishing trust within the scientific community, peer groups, and academic journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use preregistration to demonstrate commitment to rigorous methods and transparency; this helps establish trust with peers and journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximizes Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Sharing data amplifies its influence, expediting scientific progress, and communicates the reliability of your research to the wider scientific audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make data and materials available (via OSF) to increase the impact and reuse of your work; metadata connections prevent duplication of effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: (Pre)registration ensures transparency throughout the research process, preventing undisclosed modifications or selective reporting, bolstering the integrity of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record intentions, methods, and analysis plans up front to reduce selective reporting and make any later deviations clear to readers and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: By committing to a predefined plan, researchers diminish the temptation to alter methods or analyses based on observed results or external pressures, countering biases prevalent in the publish-or-perish culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a preregistered plan to limit post hoc analytic decisions and reduce incentive-driven biases (e.g., p-hacking, selective reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitates Reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A meticulously documented preregistration facilitates the reproducibility of studies, contributing significantly to the cumulative advancement of scientific knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include detailed procedures, materials, and analysis plans so others can reproduce or replicate the study; treat preregistration as part of reproducible workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced Collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective collaboration thrives when study details are transparently communicated and easily accessible to fellow researchers within the scientific community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share preregistrations and materials via OSF to lower collaboration friction and enable collaborators to understand and build on study plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamlined processes (OSF workflows)
rubrics_metrics.description: OSF takes your research materials via metadata and connects them with various tools and workflows, making it easier for you to share materials without duplicating work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage OSF's metadata and integrations to avoid duplicative tasks and to streamline sharing across tools and project components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered Reports reduce pressure for positive results
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered Reports alleviate the pressure for positive results, countering the 'file drawer problem' and promoting a more balanced and diverse literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider submitting a Registered Report to obtain in-principle acceptance based on study design rather than results, reducing incentive to produce only positive findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered Reports encourage diverse scientific practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered Reports create a platform for high-quality research beyond traditional hypothesis testing, fostering inclusivity of exploratory and confirmatory studies, enriching the scientific literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Registered Reports to legitimize and publish rigorous exploratory or unconventional study designs alongside confirmatory work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered Reports can shorten peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: For confirmatory studies, the Registered Reports format expedites the publication process. Once the study design is accepted, researchers can seamlessly progress to data collection and analysis, facilitating a shorter and more straightforward peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit study plans for peer review early (stage 1) to speed later review stages after data collection; acceptance of the protocol can streamline later publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scooping (concern) and mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Some fear that preregistration might expose their carefully crafted ideas, making them susceptible to scooping by other researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OSF reports no documented cases of stolen registrations and provides mitigations: licensing options, making registrations private for up to 4 years, and time stamps to establish priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of rigidly sticking to a research design (concern) and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Some fear (pre)registration imposes rigid constraints, limiting the ability to adapt to unexpected findings or methodological challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat preregistrations as 'a plan, not a prison' — OSF allows easy updates so researchers can document unanticipated situations and how they resolved them; clearly report deviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived applicability only to confirmatory studies (concern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some believe preregistration is only for confirmatory studies, limiting its applicability to exploratory research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preregistration is useful for exploratory work too: it documents original intentions, hypotheses, and analytical paths, increasing credibility and making clear what was exploratory versus planned (helps prevent HARKing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fear of criticism (concern) and correction mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Some are apprehensive about potential criticism from peers or reviewers when they submit a (pre)registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultural norms are shifting toward accepting mistakes; OSF allows updating preregistrations to correct errors and transparently record changes, reducing fear of critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time constraint (concern) versus upfront investment benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Some believe that all the forethought that goes with a (pre)registration takes up too much time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preparing a preregistration is an upfront investment that can streamline the study timeline by anticipating issues and avoiding mid-study pauses to resolve inconsistencies.
